snip.t: Tubal surgery, tubal ligation (a pregnancy after sterilisation is ectopic until proved otherwise), tubal reconstructive surgery

Risks and complications: Requires anaesthesia and surgery; risks include bleeding, infection, tissue injury, and rare failure (post-sterilisation pregnancies require urgent evaluation to exclude ectopic pregnancy).
Advantages: Simpler and less invasive than female sterilisation; does not affect testosterone levels, libido, erection, or ejaculation.
Methods include condoms, combined oral contraceptive pills, progestogen-only pills, injectables, implants, IUCDs, sterilisation and natural methods.

Sterilisation eliminates all microbial life including spores, whereas disinfection reduces pathogens on inanimate objects.
